# Focused code cleanup

Use this only for requested cleanup or a concrete unnecessary-complexity finding. The short engineering baseline already applies to ordinary coding; do not load this as a compulsory final stage.

Read the actual baseline-to-candidate diff and nearby conventions. Identify machinery the change adds without earning its cost: comments that paraphrase obvious code, pass-through wrappers, duplicated policy or state, placeholders, type escapes masking mismatches, or nested conditions with a simpler equivalent. Confirm what callers rely on before removing anything.

Prefer the smallest coherent simplification inside scope. A test seam, an adapter, repeated local code or a defensive check can be justified; do not delete it merely to reduce lines. Preserve external-input validation, authorization, exception causes, cancellation, transaction boundaries and useful explanations. Do not replace established fonts, colors, naming or architecture because another style feels more sophisticated. Visual direction belongs to the frontend skill when requested.

Run the relevant configured checks and behavior tests. A reviewer can make only explicitly authorized low-risk corrections; substantial redesign returns to the owner and ordinarily the original builder. Report the concrete complexity removed and evidence. No meaningful issue is a valid outcome; advisories do not restart the review loop. Use the existing result format, with a separate reviewer-authored delta when applicable.
